2. protecting pensions and the elderly at all costs, even to the point of extreme fiscal strain

now you have first and second generation immigrants, as well as young native french people, taking to the streets because the french state is hell-bent on extracting whatever it can and feeding it into the maw of boomer luxury communism.

whether the french social contract can be peacefully renegotiated remains to be seen.

$HGRAF

After spending the day doing some more research, I think protective coatings could become HydroGraph’s most profitable application.

The attraction is the combination of customer savings, meaningful graphene volumes and potential recurring demand.

For the owner of a ship, industrial plant or offshore structure, corrosion means repairs, surface preparation, labour and downtime. A coating that reduces maintenance could create savings well beyond its purchase price. That gives an effective additive a strong economic argument.

HydroGraph already has encouraging evidence. Initial Sparc laboratory tests incorporating its FGA-1 into commercial water-based coatings showed 39–60% less corrosion creep during testing lasting up to 1,680 hours. The collaboration covers further testing and potential commercial supply.

Then consider the quantities.

HydroGraph’s white paper describes 0.5% graphene in one polyurethane coating formulation, compared with 0.0015% in PET bottle testing.

For an illustrative 10,000 tonnes of finished product, those concentrations represent:

• Coating formulation: 50 tonnes of graphene
• PET formulation: 150 kg of graphene

That is approximately 333 times more graphene per tonne of finished product in the coating example.
These are separate test formulations; commercial doses and prices will vary. Still, they show why a coating application could generate substantial material demand without requiring adoption across an entire global industry.

HydroGraph’s aqueous paste also offers manufacturers a practical route into water-based formulations using standard mixing equipment.

Protective coatings could combine meaningful graphene volumes with customers willing to pay for lower maintenance costs and longer asset life. Successful formulations adopted by established manufacturers could generate repeat orders across years of production. That is why I believe a handful of commercial wins could make coatings HydroGraph’s most profitable application and a major driver of shareholder value.

Turn it off and see what breaks. Thats the valuation.
